title: It Rains Brilliants: Uncover the New Queen
summary: Move the king out of its own queen’s line, then use checking moves to finish the pawn ending.

nodes.question: Does g8=Q immediately give check?
nodes.explanation: No. Kd8 blocks the queen’s eighth-rank line to Kb8. After the source b5 reply, Ke7+ uncovers that line and forces the king toward a checked conversion.

branches.title: Independent completion: uncover check, then collect c7
commentary: Begin after the forced ...axb6 in the later source sequence. The full board retains a6/b7/c6 and Black b6/c7, with g7 ready to promote.
g8=Q is the source promotion. It does not check: White’s own king on d8 blocks the queen’s route toward b8.
b5 is the source reply. Black advances its mobile b-pawn; the c7 pawn remains blocked by c6.
Ke7+ is an independently supplied discovered check. Moving Kd8 opens the queen’s eighth rank toward Kb8.
Ka7 is forced. The white b7 pawn controls a8/c8 and the queen controls the eighth rank.
Qb8+ checks diagonally on a7 while keeping the queen beside the advanced pawns.
Kb6 is one legal retreat. Black’s other legal reply here captures a6, which is shown separately.
Qxc7+ captures c7 and reaches an exact seven-piece White win. White keeps a6/b7/c6 and Black keeps b5; no spare pawn is dropped to fit the tablebase.
branches.classification: source g8=Q/b5; subsequent moves independently supplied representative completion
branches.explanation: Qxc7+ captures c7 and reaches an exact seven-piece White win. White keeps a6/b7/c6 and Black keeps b5; no spare pawn is dropped to fit the tablebase.

branches.title: Independent defense: capture the a6 pawn
commentary: Compare the other king response to the checking queen move. Only the opening promotion and b5 are taken from the source.
g8=Q promotes without check because Kd8 interrupts the eighth rank.
b5 moves the black pawn forward and leaves White a discovered check.
Ke7+ clears d8 so Qg8 checks the king on b8.
Ka7 is the sole legal response to that discovered check.
Qb8+ checks Ka7 and forces a king move.
Kxa6 captures the white a-pawn and reaches seven pieces. Exact tablebase evidence still gives White a win; the result is checked after the actual capture rather than inferred from having a queen.

branches.title: Independent defense: move the king before the pawn
commentary: Test the other legal reply to g8=Q instead of assuming ...b5 is forced.
g8=Q promotes. The queen’s line toward b8 is still blocked by Kd8.
Ka7 is a legal independent alternative to b5. It leaves c7 available to the white king.
Kxc7 captures the blocked c-pawn, reaching an exact seven-piece White win with a6/b7/c6 and Black b6 retained.

exercises.prompt: Why is Ke7 written with a check sign?
exercises.answer: It uncovers Qg8’s line across the eighth rank to Kb8. The king is not itself checking the opposing king.

exercises.prompt: Which original black pawn ends up on b6?
exercises.answer: The a7 pawn captures the white b6 pawn. The complete later board therefore contains a black b6 pawn and no black a7 pawn.

startContext: Begin after ...axb6, immediately before g8=Q at 175 seconds, with the complete eight-piece later diagram: White Kd8/a6/b7/c6/g7 against Kb8/b6/c7. The source promotion and b5 reply are visible; subsequent king routes and captures are explicitly independent representative completions. A finite legal strategy covers every Black defense after g8=Q and ends in exact seven-piece wins. Earlier queen sacrifice, knight route, rook blockade, king march and pawn diversion remain outside this proof. The b6 pawn is the black a7 pawn after axb6, not a missing spare pawn.
